output: AURA is an autonomous AI ecosystem that integrates multiple AMEs (Autonomous Modular Entities) to provide intelligent assistance across various domains.

text: How do I create a new AME?
output: To create a new AME, use the /api/ame-core endpoint with a POST request containing the AME configuration. The system will initialize and register the new entity.
AURA currently supports 5 integrations: Slack, Discord, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, and Webhooks. Each can be configured via the /api/integrations endpoint.

text: How does the analytics dashboard work?
output: The analytics dashboard provides real-time metrics on system performance, including event counts, error rates, latency, and integration health. Data is aggregated every hour.
Yes! AURA supports local deployment via the autonomous-setup.ps1 script. It sets up the backend on localhost:8000 with SQLite for development.
AURA uses a microservices architecture with a FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, and multiple integration points. The system is designed for scalability and modularity.

text: How do I monitor system health?
output: The /api/health endpoint provides real-time health checks. Additionally, the monitoring system logs all events and alerts on anomalies.
AURA supports PostgreSQL for production and SQLite for development. Firebase is used for real-time features and authentication.
Authentication uses Firebase Auth with JWT tokens. The frontend handles login/signup, and the backend validates tokens for protected endpoints.
An AME (Autonomous Modular Entity) is a specialized AI agent within the AURA ecosystem. Each AME has specific capabilities and can communicate with other AMEs.

text: How do I deploy to Vercel?
output: Deploy to Vercel by connecting your GitHub repository. The auto-deploy workflow in .github/workflows/auto-deploy.yml handles CI/CD automatically.

text: What is the API rate limit?
output: The API rate limit is configured in frontend/lib/rateLimit.ts. Default is 100 requests per minute per user. Contact support for custom limits.

text: How do I add a new integration?
output: Add a new integration by creating a service module in the backend, adding the API route, and configuring the frontend component. See docs/INTEGRATIONS.md.
AURA uses a combination of health checks, logging, and the analytics engine. The system monitors latency, error rates, and usage patterns.
Offline sync uses AsyncStorage to queue requests. When the connection is restored, the sync engine processes the queue and updates the server.
Backups are configured via AURA_Core/backup_system.py. The system supports automated backups to local storage and cloud services.

text: How do I configure environment variables?
output: Copy .env.example to .env.local and fill in your credentials. Key variables include API keys, database URLs, and Firebase config.
The frontend uses Jest for unit tests and end-to-end tests. The backend uses pytest. Tests are in the tests/ directory.

text: How does the event bus work?
output: The event bus (AURA_Core/event_bus.py) enables communication between AMEs. Events are published and subscribed to via a publish-subscribe pattern.
The deployment pipeline uses GitHub Actions. On push to main, it runs tests, builds, and deploys to Vercel automatically.

text: Help me set up the backend
output: Run .\scripts\autonomous-setup.ps1 in PowerShell. This will install dependencies, configure the database, and start the server on localhost:8000.
401 errors indicate authentication issues. Make sure your Firebase token is valid and included in the Authorization header as Bearer <token>.

text: How do I reset my password?
output: Use the forgot password flow in the login screen. A password reset email will be sent to your registered email address.
Check that the backend is running on localhost:8000. Run the health check at /api/health. If the backend is down, restart with autonomous-setup.ps1.

text: How do I add a new user?
output: New users can sign up through the frontend login page. Admin users can also create users via the Firebase console.

text: What should I do if sync fails?
output: Check your internet connection first. If the issue persists, try manual sync in Settings. The system will automatically retry every 30 seconds.
Pull the latest changes from GitHub: git pull origin main. Then run npm install and restart the backend. Check CHANGELOG.md for breaking changes.
Check the analytics dashboard for performance metrics. Common issues include high latency on the backend or network congestion.
Use the /api/analytics endpoint to export metrics. For full data export, contact support or use the Firebase console.
Yes! The frontend uses Next.js with Tailwind CSS. You can customize components in frontend/app/ and styles in the respective CSS files.
